sections.html:
Northbrook is one of the simpler Cook County villages to sell in on paper, because it charges no municipal transfer tax and issues no transfer stamps. The one local step is closing out the water account with a final meter reading.

The village sits on the North Shore and has 34,744 residents (July 2025 estimate). Housing is mostly owner-occupied (87.2%) and high in value, with a median owner-occupied value of $652,300, so most of a seller's effort goes into pricing and condition. About 91.9% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which means few homes change hands in a given year and comparable sales can be thin on a specific block. Ask an agent or appraiser for nearby sales, since the village median hides block-by-block differences.

Northbrook does not levy a real estate transfer tax or issue transfer stamps, and the Cook County Clerk's municipal transfer tax list has no entry for the village.

The state and county taxes still apply, with the seller as the liable party. The state rate comes from 35 ILCS 200/31-10. A sale also needs the PTAX-203 transfer declaration.

Transfer charges on a Northbrook sale
ChargeRateWho is liable
State of Illinois50 cents per $500Seller
Cook County25 cents per $500Seller
Village of NorthbrookNoneNot applicable

Northbrook Municipal Code Section 27-63 requires everyone in a property transaction to confirm with the village that a final meter reading was taken and that no unpaid water balance remains. Call the water billing office at 847-664-4171 to set that up.

  • Water is billed quarterly, and sewer and stormwater charges ride on the same bill.
  • If the seller leaves a balance, the code ties it to the property, and it moves to the new owner's account after thirty days.
  • Close any utility accounts and schedule final reads as part of the sale.

Settling the final bill at the closing table avoids a dispute with the buyer later. For liens and other debts, search the Cook County Property Tax Portal. Its records may not be complete, so a FOIA request to the village for building permits and other outstanding items on a parcel is a sensible extra check.

Most of Northbrook lies in Northfield Township, and a northwest corner lies in Wheeling Township. Both are north suburb townships on the Cook County Assessor's triennial reassessment cycle.

Look up your parcel's township and 14-digit PIN on the Assessor's site. The township assessor for Northfield can answer questions about an appeal. For installment dates and the balance on a parcel, ask the Cook County Treasurer, because the closing statement usually prorates the bill.

Several elementary districts, numbered 27, 28, 30 and 31, serve the village, and High School District 225 feeds Glenbrook North High School. A small northwest corner falls in Wheeling's District 21, and a southeast sliver is in Sunset Ridge District 29. Because district boundaries cross house by house, a listing should name the exact elementary and junior high district for the address. The village's Know Your Neighborhood tool shows zoning and school districts by property.

Metra's Milwaukee District North Line stops at Northbrook station on Shermer Road downtown, and shopping runs along Sanders Road, Skokie Boulevard and Lake Cook Road. Mean travel time to work is 26.8 minutes, so name the train and the main roads in a listing.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Cook County
sections.html:
Northbrook deeds are recorded through the Cook County Clerk's recordings office at 118 N. Clark St., phone 312.603.5050, which also lists the state and county stamp amounts. A rubber stamp is the proof of payment.

Because Northbrook has no municipal stamp, the closing package is lighter than in many neighboring suburbs. You still need a signed deed, the PTAX-203 declaration, clear title and a final water read. If a trust or estate holds the title, the title company will tell you which exemption language applies.

At these prices, most Northbrook houses sell through a standard listing, since buyers usually arrive with a mortgage. A direct sale makes sense when the house needs more work than a listing can absorb or a family needs a quick, quiet close.

  • Choose a listing when the house is updated and you can wait for showings.
  • Choose a direct cash sale when the property is dated, a tenant or estate issue slows a listing, or you need a firm closing date.
  • Either way, arrange the final water read, confirm liens through the Cook County portal, and order the PTAX-203.

With no village stamp to wait on, the Northbrook side of a quick sale can move fast: book the water read, gather the deed and declaration, and let the title company handle recording.

Put four items in one folder: the latest Cook County tax bill with your PIN, your loan payoff statement if you have a mortgage, the water account details, and any permit records for additions or major work. A buyer's attorney will ask for most of these, and the title company needs them to prorate the tax bill.

Call 847-664-4171 as soon as you have a closing date so the final reading lands on or near it. If the title is in a trust or estate, send the trust certificate or letters of office to the title company early so the deed language is settled before the closing table.

faqs.q: Does Northbrook have a real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The village does not levy a transfer tax or issue transfer stamps. State and Cook County transfer taxes still apply on the deed.

faqs.q: What must I do about the water bill when I sell?
faqs.a: Call 847-664-4171 to schedule a final meter reading and pay the balance. Section 27-63 of the municipal code requires the final read, and any unpaid amount moves to the new owner after thirty days.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Northbrook houses?
faqs.a: Elementary districts 27, 28, 30 and 31 serve most of the village, and District 225's Glenbrook North High School serves most of it. Small areas fall in Wheeling's District 21 or Sunset Ridge District 29, so check the exact address.

faqs.q: Which township assessor handles my Northbrook property?
faqs.a: Most of the village is in Northfield Township and a corner is in Wheeling Township. Look up your PIN on the Cook County Assessor's site to confirm the township.

faqs.q: How do I check for liens before listing?
faqs.a: Use Cook County's Property Tax Portal to search for liens or debts on the parcel. Its records may not be complete, so a FOIA request to the village for building permits and other debts is a good second check.
